subject: Hospitality
title: Greek Xenía: The Sacred Duty
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Greek Xenía: The Sacred Duty.

hook.text: In ancient Greece, refusing a stranger shelter wasn't just rude—it was an offense against Zeus himself.

buildup.text: Xenía was the sacred law of hospitality. Hosts had to offer food, drink, a bath, and gifts before even asking a guest's name.

discovery.text: The Odyssey is built on xenía. Every episode tests whether hosts and guests honor or violate this sacred code.

twist.text: Guests had obligations too. Overstaying, being rude, or betraying a host was equally punishable by the gods.

climax.text: The word 'hospitality' derives from Latin 'hospes,' itself descended from Greek xenia—a 3,000-year-old ethical chain.

punchline.text: Hospitality began as a divine law, not a business model.

quiz.question: What was xenía in ancient Greece?
options: The sacred law of hospitality, protected by Zeus
